title: Library-backed JSON hidden behind typed adapters

nodes.summary: UTF-8 JSON over a private synchronous protocol, using existing libraries
nodes.detail: Host and guest exchange UTF-8 JSON over a small private synchronous protocol: Aeson on the host and an existing guest JSON library chosen by a conformance proof. Kyyn does not write another parser; if no library passes, the decision reopens.

realised.evidence: PR #6 ships the private guest runtime using unchanged json library parsing/printing with Aeson on the host

nodes.summary: Generated adapters own the wire; authored code never sees JSON
nodes.detail: SDK-generated adapters own serialization, framing, request IDs, dispatch, contract matching and structured failures; ordinary KB/plugin code never sees Value, JSON text, pipes or envelopes. The host translates disk values and never sends executable Dhall.

realised.evidence: Generated codecs at PR #6, and generated query adapters at PR #27 keep wire values out of authored queries

nodes.summary: Private request/response envelopes; undeclared errors abort, never reach continuations
nodes.detail: Guest messages are HostRequest or Completed; host replies HostResponse with a declared HostCallError or value. Recoverable errors must be part of the request's declared result type; envelope-level errors abort the invocation rather than being cast into the continuation's x or an empty page.

realised.evidence: PR #96 implements HostRequest/HostResponse envelopes with strict response decoding before continuation resumption

nodes.summary: Adapter checks method availability and contracts before dispatch and reply
nodes.detail: The host adapter resolves each request's method among the invocation's available capabilities, checks input against the descriptor, dispatches, then checks output against the result contract; the guest decoder reconstructs the exact suspended x. A matching response ID is not a type check.

realised.evidence: PR #99's protocol broker rejects unknown handles, methods and request IDs and out-of-row requests before effects

nodes.summary: Pure library-backed frame codec, separate from the contract checker
nodes.detail: decodeFrame/encodeFrame validate envelope syntax via a library parser/encoder only; capability availability and KB semantics are elsewhere, and the contract checker (ADR 0005) separately produces CheckedValue.

realised.evidence: decodeFrame code_added at seq 80 (PR #99 native broker)

nodes.summary: One compact JSON object per LF-terminated frame; stdout protocol-only
nodes.detail: Each message is a single compact JSON line (library encoding escapes newlines), avoiding the prototype's byte-counting transport; stdout carries only protocol and stderr diagnostics.

realised.evidence: PR #96's plugin adapter exercises LF framing over real pipes under GHC and MicroHs

nodes.summary: Restricted value profile: decimal strings, tagged unions and optionals
nodes.detail: Integers/decimals travel as canonical decimal strings (never Double), unions and optionals as explicit tags, identities/dates as documented strings for recognised library types only, large binaries as typed references; no functions, NaN, omitted-field defaults or union guessing.

realised.evidence: PR #6 generated codecs round-trip arbitrary-precision integer strings, nested optionals and tagged unions between GHC/Aeson and MicroHs

nodes.summary: Duplicate-key decoding behaviour pinned consistently across both peers
nodes.detail: Generated frames have unique fields; the decoder's duplicate-key policy must be pinned and identical on host and guest (rejection preferred only if libraries allow it without another scanner). No semantic JSON hashing or extra approval identity.

realised.evidence: Guest runtime Json.hs (PR #6) normalises keys before structural decoding

nodes.summary: Adapters generated in lockstep; no version negotiation, one outstanding request
nodes.detail: Kyyn generates both adapters for its installed runtime with no protocol/SDK negotiation; protocol changes update both together. One outstanding request per guest; unknown methods, mismatched identities and out-of-order messages fail before any effect, and changed contracts yield a repair instruction.

realised.evidence: PR #96 conversational adapter handles one request at a time and aborts on wrong IDs/tags before resuming

nodes.summary: Outer invocation owns nested plugin calls, their cancellation and resources
nodes.detail: A parent KB may synchronously call a plugin in a separate invocation (no recursive call graph); the outer invocation owns child processes, cancellation releases them, recoverable errors return typed, and per-call processes suffice without pooling.

realised.evidence: PR #107 KB tools start one captured-method guest per call from the tool invocation, without a process pool; cancellation propagation not separately evidenced

nodes.summary: Aeson 2.2.5.0 host; unchanged json-0.11 Types/String modules on MicroHs
nodes.detail: The guest library is selected: unchanged Text.JSON.Types and Text.JSON.String from json-0.11 compile under pinned MicroHs, with no umbrella module, alternate backend or parser fork; upstream notices are preserved.

realised.evidence: PR #5 only probed; PR #6 vendors pinned upstream sources and uses them in the guest runtime

nodes.summary: Kyyn generates JSON mappings from compiler-inspected authored ADTs
nodes.detail: Generated structural codecs map library JSON values to constructors/fields of supported, compiler-inspected ADTs, checking tags, fields and payload types; authors maintain neither codecs nor a second schema, and mappings need real MicroHs round-trip tests.

realised.evidence: PR #6 implements compiler-inspected ADT codec generation with real MicroHs round trips

nodes.summary: Decoded-value checks reject surrogates, JSON numbers and nulls
nodes.detail: After parsing and before dispatch or encoding, retained strings and keys are checked recursively for surrogate Chars, and numeric/null nodes are rejected; these are decoded-value checks, not another syntax scanner or canonical-frame service.

realised.evidence: Guest Json.hs (PR #6) rejects JSNull, JSRational and surrogate characters

nodes.summary: Duplicate keys resolved first-key-wins, matching Aeson 2.2.5.0
nodes.detail: Both peers use first-key-wins per object; the guest normalises its association lists (recursively) before structural decoding, and dependency updates must rerun this conformance assertion.

realised.evidence: firstKeys normalisation in guest Json.hs from the PR #6 runtime

nodes.summary: Newtypes use ordinary constructor mapping; no name-based transparency
nodes.detail: Positional wrappers are tagged and named record wrappers are objects; transparency is never inferred from a type's name or newtype-ness, and string representations apply only to recognised SDK/library scalars, not a KB type called FactId or Date.

realised.evidence: PR #6 tests ordinary newtype wrappers in real MicroHs round trips

nodes.summary: Concrete plugin envelope: typed Either result, canonical integer request IDs
nodes.detail: The plugin adapter starts with {arguments, snapshot}, emits tagged HostRequest/Completed objects and receives HostResponse whose result encodes the typed Either FetchError a directly, without a second error wrapper. Wrong IDs, tags, fields or payloads abort before resumption; config/payload codecs come from inspected types.

realised.evidence: PR #96 implements and tests this envelope under GHC and MicroHs against a recording broker

nodes.summary: Chunk-framed binary sections replace LF-terminated JSON lines
nodes.detail: Each section is a series of chunks (canonical ASCII byte count, LF, exact bytes; max 64 KiB) ended by a zero-length chunk; receivers reject oversize, noncanonical or truncated input, and chunk boundaries carry no meaning. Motivated by issue #199 throughput measurements.

realised.evidence: PR #202 implements two length-prefixed chunk sections per message with 64 KiB maximum chunks and explicit terminators (Transport.hs)

nodes.summary: Frames carry JSON metadata plus a raw body used only for HTTP
nodes.detail: Frame = metadata + body; decodeMessage also validates the permitted body. HTTP request/response bodies (any status) travel raw instead of as escaped JSON strings; transport failures have no body and other messages reject a nonempty one.

realised.evidence: PR #202: HTTP request/response bodies bypass the nested JSON string, including non-2xx responses

nodes.summary: Verified binary standard handles per platform; no text-mode fallback
nodes.detail: The guest reads exact chunks with native block I/O and must obtain binary stdin/stdout under GHC and MicroHs on Linux, macOS and WSL; reopening /dev/stdin|stdout needs platform verification and silently falling back to text mode is forbidden.

realised.evidence: PR #202 adds native block I/O and binary handles (Transport.hs uses /dev/stdout and hSetBinaryMode); macOS/WSL verification not evidenced

nodes.summary: Guest retains packed Text/ByteString and encodes results in bounded pieces
nodes.detail: SDK identities, messages and textual payloads use Text, with String conversion local to adapters; results are encoded and written incrementally while still forming one terminal Completed message, with no per-page result protocol.

realised.evidence: PR #202: SDK identifiers/payloads use Text and terminal JSON is emitted in bounded pieces with one Completed result

editorial.note: Progress prose: native broker now interprets filesystem and evidence requests; no requirement change.
Progress prose: registration and configured acquisition proved.
Drops the 'no multi-version protocol or historical evidence schema negotiation' clause after ADR 0014 went latest-only; 'no protocol/SDK version negotiation' remains in 0007.09.
Navigation/link updates (vendored inputs, codec tests) and rewording of the MicroHs round-trip requirement already covered by 0007.12.

Desired-state reconciliation: removes status/basis, rewords context and decimal-mapping gate as firm rules covered by 0007.07, and restates broker dispatch by selected row (covered by 0007.04 and ADR 0009).

notes: Founding decision had no ### subsections; it was split by commitment across 'Decision proposed', 'Proposed value profile' and 'Protocol boundary' (10 nodes). The lane is short and stable: the only real reversal is framing, where LF-terminated JSON lines (seq 1, used from seq 78) were replaced by chunk-framed binary sections with raw HTTP bodies (seq 154) after a measured throughput problem (issue #199), implemented the next step (seq 155). Seq 5 is where the proposal became concrete: library choice plus decoded-value checks that were added to work around json-0.11 surrogate/leading-zero bugs rather than patching the library. Seq 1's verification and protocol-boundary text promised nested plugin-call cancellation; I found only indirect evidence (per-call method guests in KB tools, PR #107), so 0007.10 is low confidence. Platform portability of binary handles (0007.19) is explicitly a requirement whose macOS/WSL verification is not asserted.
